questions: Are you having pain in either knee?
Is the pain worse when walking or climbing stairs?
Have you had this knee problem for more than a month?
Is one knee worse than the other?
Have you noticed swelling, warmth, or redness around either knee?
Do your knees feel stiff after sitting or when you first wake up?
Have your knees ever locked or given way?
Have you fallen because of your knees?
Did the symptoms begin after an injury?
Do you have pain in other joints as well?
Do you have fever or feel unwell?
Have you had previous surgery or injections in either knee?
Do you have numbness or weakness in either leg?
Is the pain severe even when you are resting?
orders: Observe the patient’s gait, balance, and ability to rise from the chair and walk.
Examine both knees for alignment, deformity, swelling, tenderness, warmth, and range of motion.
Assess active and passive knee extension and flexion, including for fixed flexion contractures.
Perform manual muscle testing of hip, knee, and ankle movements bilaterally.
Perform a focused neurologic examination of both lower limbs, including reflexes, sensation, and coordination.
Assess distal lower-limb pulses and capillary refill.
served: deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses
